ERC-7540 (Final, Created 2023-10-18, CC0-1.0) mandates no rounding direction for a partial claim, which is why two vectors run the same claim sequence under both declared directions and differ.

dust.note: A stranded amount is one side of a claimable bucket left non-zero after the other side reached zero, so no further claim against it can be computed at the bucket's rate.

invariants.name: pending_and_claimable_disjoint
invariants.source: ERC-7540: pendingDepositRequest/claimableDepositRequest (and the redeem pair) each exclude the other state's amount.
invariants.detail: Structural: this kernel models pending and claimable as separate buckets and never moves an amount between them, so the two views can never double-count. A claim only ever draws from the claimable bucket.

invariants.name: claim_never_skips_claimable_state
invariants.source: ERC-7540: "Requests MUST NOT skip or otherwise short-circuit the Claim state."
invariants.detail: Every claim drew only from an amount already in the Claimable state.

invariants.name: claim_within_claimable_bounds
invariants.source: ERC-7540 max* views track the claimable amount (the standard notes maxDeposit moves in sync with claimableDepositRequest).
invariants.detail: No claim exceeded its leg's remaining claimable amount.

invariants.name: single_prorata_rate_for_nonzero_request_id
invariants.source: ERC-7540: "If a Request with requestId != 0 becomes partially claimable, all requests of the same requestId MUST become claimable at the same pro-rata rate."
invariants.detail: Not applicable: request_id is 0, the aggregate-by-controller convention, where amounts from separate requests are fungible and no single per-request rate is asserted.

invariants.name: partial_claim_rounding_direction_is_declared_not_mandated
invariants.source: ERC-7540 states no rounding direction for a partial claim. ERC-4626 fixes a direction per function; ERC-7540 does not extend that to claims.
invariants.detail: Direction "down" was supplied by the caller, not derived from the standard. Each claim reports what the opposite direction would have produced.

output_payload.note: Recomputes ERC-7540 asynchronous-vault request accounting from caller-declared request state: applies a sequence of claims against the claimable buckets at the implied pro-rata rate, tracks the pending/claimable/claimed split, and checks the standard's stated invariants (pending and claimable are disjoint views; a claim never skips the Claim state; a non-zero requestId stays at one pro-rata rate). ERC-7540 mandates NO rounding direction for a partial claim, so the direction here is a declared parameter and the result of the opposite direction is reported alongside it. This kernel does NOT read any chain: it cannot know whether the declared amounts match any deployed vault, when or whether a pending request will be fulfilled (the standard leaves that timing unspecified), whether the controller is authorised, or whether a claim transaction would succeed.
